sets.g: Passage A represents a formal and polite invitation to a wedding. The language is also precise, and it contains details of the event. Passage B represents a less formal invitation to a wedding. It seems like a personal message to the recipient and is somewhat playful. As such, the response is perhaps familiar and friendly in return.
sets.p:
A. Together with both families, we request the honour of your presence at our wedding on Monday, the first of January, at nine o’clock. Ceremony followed by reception.
B. As you may know, we are getting married! This invite is to let you know that we expect you there. It wouldn’t be the same without you.
i: Thanks for the invite, I’ll be there. I’ll see you at the reception where we can catch up.
B
This response indicates that the recipient and responder know each other. ‘Thanks,’ is also a most casual form of gratitude. This fits in with category B easily.
It is with the greatest of pleasure that I accept your invitation. The honour shall be mine.
A
The language is flowery, if a little archaic. Extremely formal language which is only fit for category A.
Why, of course I shall be attending! I could not imagine any alternative. Send my love to the family.
B

Whilst the language is eloquent and somewhat formal, it is intimate. The last phrase suggests that the responder is a family friend which indicates that this response is much more appropriate to passage B.
Please accept my delicate decline as I will be unable to attend your wedding in January.
A
The language is very formal and distant – sent from someone perhaps not too familiar with the invitees. Therefore, this response is for passage A.
With great sorrow, I must politely refuse your offer. It would be too difficult for me to attend given our complicated circumstances.
A
The language is polite and formal. This is a more appropriate response to a formal invitation which is passage A.

sets.p: Thank you to all who could / should / would make our wedding last week. We were very happy with the ceremony and the reception. Each one of you had / have a role to play and we are ever so grateful that you were there. I would furthermore / anymore like to extend my thanks for your gifts. They will help immensely once we / you move into our new home in Bedford. I send my love to you all / only / both. We are soon to leave for our honeymoon – to the island of Bora Bora! It has been a / the / our long time coming.
i: “Thank you to all who (could / should / would) make our wedding last week”
Could
Should
Would
A

‘Should’ and ‘would’ do not work well grammatically, as they do not fit in the past tense without changing the succeeding word ‘make.’ ‘Could’ is the only option that works properly, as it implies that the message is directed to those who were able to attend. As such, it is the correct answer.
“Each one of you (had / have) a role to play…”
Had
Have
A
‘Have’ places the sentence in the present tense, for which the message is not. ‘Had’ puts it in past tense, which is correct as the wedding was an event that has already happened and is in the past.
“I would (anymore / furthermore) like to extend my thanks for your gifts.”
Anymore
Furthermore
B

‘I would anymore’ does not make grammatical sense and therefore cannot be correct. On the other hand, ‘furthermore’ is to continue the conversation, which is the case in this passage. Therefore, ‘furthermore’ is the correct answer.
“They will help immensely once (we / you) move into our new home in Bedford.”
We
You
A

While the sentence works with ‘you’, it changes the meaning to something quite confusing. The passage is focused on the wedding, and to immediately direct it to the reader is confusing and unlikely. ‘We’ focuses on the writer of the letter which is the subject of the passage throughout. Therefore, this is the correct answer.
“I send my love to you (all / both / only).”
All
Both
Only
A

‘Only’ is peculiar in this context and quite rude. Given the open message, this is highly unlikely. ‘Both’ works, but would suggest that the message is only sent to two people. Again, given the open nature of the message, it indicates that it is a message sent to all invitees of the wedding – which will be more than two otherwise, ‘both’ or ‘you two’ might have appeared somewhere earlier in the message. ‘All’ works best and is the most appropriate given the context.
“It has been (a / our / the) long time coming.
A
Our
The
A
‘Our’ and ‘the’ do not particularly make much sense. In this case, ‘a’ is the only possible solution which completes the well-known phrase, ‘a long time coming’.

sets.p: As many of you will be aware, I have known my fiancé for many years know. We both attended university together studying geographie. I care about my fiancé deeply as we have shared many great moments together and weathered many tribulations. However, I am worried that I am leaving my youth behind. I still feel youth, and I want to experience the world without the burden of company. I do not know how to do and I need your support and guidance. What would I do?
i: “I have known my fiancé for many years know.”
Now
Need to delete the ‘k’ to change the word ‘know’, which makes no sense in this context, to now which is correct by saying how long the narrator knows the fiancé.
“We both attended university together studying geographie.”
Geography
There is a spelling mistake with ‘geographie’ which needs to be corrected to ‘geography’.
“I still feel youth…”
Youthful
This does not make grammatical sense. The word ‘youth’ needs to be changed to an adjective, in this case, ‘youthful’.
“I do not know how to do”
What
‘How’ does not make sense in this sentence. The correct word is ‘what’ as in, ‘what to do’.
“What would I do?
Should

While ‘would’ works, given the context seems strange. The message is asking for advice, therefore, the more appropriate word is ‘should’. This would change to ‘what should I do?’ which is the correct answer in this case.

sets.p:
Presented are the responses someone has received from friends, family and acquaintances regarding a personal issue they had sought for support and guidance.

1. Everybody feels this way. Do not worry, you will get through this momentary lapse.
2. I am sorry to hear about your hesitations, though I cannot say I am surprised.
3. I am shocked you did not feel like this earlier, as I have always felt you two were doomed to fail.
4. You are surrounded by love and support, no matter what happens, you will get through these tough moments.
5. My dear, I can see why you may feel this way. However, I believe in your strength to overcome this difficult time.
i: Everybody feels this way. Do not worry, you will get through this momentary lapse.
3rd

This response is warm and kind. It does not however provide a positive message, but insists the person is doing wrong but it will be righted. There are other responses that are kinder, as such, this ranks in the middle with 3rd place.
I am sorry to hear about your hesitations, though I cannot say I am surprised.
4th
This response is surprisingly callous and quite negative. It is not the most negative, however, as there is worse. Therefore, this ranks 4th.
I am shocked you did not feel like this earlier, as I have always felt you two were doomed to fail.
5th
This response is mean and evidently the most negative. Explicitly stated that the two partners were doomed to fail is very harsh. Therefore, this ranks 5th.
You are surrounded by love and support, no matter what happens, you will get through these tough moments.
1st
This response shows much affection, especially with using words ‘love’ and ‘support’. This is giving maximum reassurance and is the most positive message here.
My dear, I can see why you may feel this way. However, I believe in your strength to overcome this difficult time.
2nd
This response is tender and offers encouragement. Clearly one of the more positive messages, though it is not the most tender, as we have seen with the answer to Q4.4. Therefore, this ranks as B.

sets.p: We shall meet at Manor Farm for the wedding reception. This is 2 miles from St. Matthew’s Church, where the ceremony will be held. For people willing to walk the distance, this should take you 25-30 minutes – so plan accordingly. There will be a choice of dinner menus at the reception – vegan options are available. Drinks, both alcoholic and non-alcoholic, are on the house, so celebrate our gathering with joyous occasion!
i: The distance from St. Matthew’s Church to Manor Farm is 3 miles.
False
False – The second line in the passage states that it is 2 miles distance.
The wedding ceremony will be held at Manor Farm.
False
False - The second line in the passage states that the wedding ceremony will be held at St Matthew’s Church – not to be confused with the wedding reception held at Manor Farm. Therefore, it is false.
A guest can have 2 glasses of wine with their dinner.
True
True – The fifth line states that attendees may purchase drinks. Since this is possible, a guest can simply purchase two glasses of wine for dinner if they so choose.
It will take an average of 27 minutes to walk from St. Matthews Church to Manor Farm.
Cannot Say
Cannot Say - There is no mention of what the average walking time from St. Matthews Church to Manor Farm. Therefore, we cannot say.
Most guests will be driving from the wedding ceremony to the reception.
Cannot Say
Cannot say – There is no mention of this information in the passage. Therefore, we cannot say.

sets.g: Passage A represents a formal and considered message. The language is formal and professional. The response to this message must equally be formal and kindly, though perhaps distant and deferential. Passage B represents a less formal message to the applicant. Equally positive, it is more familiar and casual. It is likely that the sender and the submitter know each other at least a little bit. As such, the response is perhaps slightly bold, familiar in return.
sets.p:
A. Having carefully listened through all the submissions, we have concluded as anonymous voters that your track is the winner. Congratulations. Please reply to this message within the next 7 days.
B. Your submission was clearly better than the others we received – so it should be obvious at this point that you are in fact the winner! Nice work. Give me a call over the next few days to discuss details.
i: Oh wow, that is great news, give my thanks the all those who voted.
B
The language is very informal. As such, it is quite inappropriate a response for passage A but not so for passage B. Therefore, this is a response for passage B.
Cheers for that! I’ll give you a shout when I get a moment at lunch.
B
This response infers that the sender and applicant known each other well. They have an equal status, and the language is very casual = B
It humbles me considerably upon hearing such glorious news. You do me a great honour.
A
The language is quite flowery but polite. The phrase is also filled with adjectives of praise. This response suits passage A.
Thank you for your vote of confidence. I shall do my utmost to provide a wonderful track for you.
A
The language is polite, formal and reserved. It is much more appropriate from employee to employer rather than close friends. As such, this response fits passage A.
Thanks for your response. I promise I will not let you down.
B

While this response could potentially work for both passages, as it is fairly neutral, it suggests a more casual style. The word ‘thanks’ does not seem formal enough for passage A and not ‘letting you down’ suggests a more personal note that does not work with distance. Therefore, this is better suited for passage B.

sets.p: Thank you for you / your / you’re feedback regarding the track. I think I see what needs do / doing / done. The introduction sequence is energetic, and the track needs to reflect that. I am going to shorten the ambient beginning and get straight / strait / strate to the beat after 8 seconds, instead of 12. The hi-hats need a big reduce / reducing / reduction in high-end frequencies as they can grate the ear after repeated listens. Finally, the fade-out is ineffective. He / I / Our suggest a synchronised crash over the last few frames. That should create greater impact.
i: “Thank you for (your / you’re / you) feedback regarding the track…”
You
Your
You’re
B

‘You’ does not make sense in this context. ‘You’re’ means ‘you are’, to say ‘you are feedback’ is not correct under these circumstances – nor really in any. Therefore, the correct answer is ‘your’ – ‘thank you for YOUR feedback’ – explaining that the feedback is theirs.
“I think I see what needs (doing / done / to do).”
Doing
Done
To Do
A

Here the possible answers are variations on ‘do’. The infinitive ‘to do’ is grammatically incorrect in this sense, since it is not conjugated to fit the sentence. ‘Done’ is past tense which in this context, talking of the future, does not work. ‘Doing’ allows the sentence to make sense by describing ‘what needs doing’.
“…get (straight / strait) to the beat…”
Straight
Strait
Strate
A

Here is a confusion with the same sounding, and closely spelled word. A ‘strait’ is a narrow passage of water that connects two seas. Clearly, it is not meant for this passage. A ‘strate’ is not a word in the English language, but has a similar sound to the other two. What we require is ‘straight’, used as a synonym for ‘immediately’.
The hi-hats need a big (reduce / reducing / reduction) in high-end frequencies
Reduce
Reducing
Reduction
C

The answers are variations on a similar word ‘to reduce’. Both ‘reduce’ and ‘reducing’ do not aptly describe the situation. They are conjugated incorrectly. ‘Reduction’ describes that the object or subject is reduced. Therefore, this is the correct answer.
“(He / I / our) suggest a synchronised crash over the last few frames.”
He
I
Our
B

‘He’ suggest a’ would work only if ‘suggest’ was correctly conjugated to ‘suggests’. As such, ‘he’ does not work. ‘Our suggest,’ likewise has a conjugation problem, as in this situation is should be ‘suggestion’, or this could also be viewed to be using the object form of the pronoun rather than the subject form; ‘we.’ However, ‘I suggest’ works correctly, and as such is the right answer.

sets.p: Having listened to the latest version of the trailer, I must confess that I am dishappy. Your track, while no doubt musical interesting, derails the vibe that I feel the trailer should create. It was meant to be frantic and aggressive, yet your music somewho subdues the energy into something sinister and brooding. This is not really what I am look for. I think we need to take another look at this thing and I am asking you to come up for something more fitting to my design.
i: “I must confess that I am dishappy.”
Unhappy
‘Dishappy’ is not a real word. It is a nonsense attempt at a negation of happy. The correct, and real word used is ‘unhappy’.
“Your track, while no doubt musical interesting…”
Musically
‘Musical’ is not grammatical describing the track. It needs to be conjugated to ‘musically’.
“…yet your music somewho subdues the energy…”
Somehow
‘Somewho’ is not a real word, and needs to be replaced and corrected by ‘somehow’. ‘Somehow’ is used to wonder but confirm that the music subdues the energy but we are not sure why.
“This is not really what I am look for.”
Looking

‘Look’ needs to be changed from the present tense to the present continuous tense in order to explain this situation is ongoing (continuous). Therefore, ‘look’ needs to change to ‘looking’ which would result in = ‘ what I am looking for’.
“…I am asking you to come up for something…”
With
Given the context, the object being devised is not for something. Instead, the individual needs to come up ‘with’ something that the director is looking for. Therefore, the correct answer is ‘with’.

sets.p:
Shown are responses you have received from various people regarding their thoughts and criticisms of a proposal you had put forward to the company director.

1. I am impressed with what you have done here. I cannot quite see what the director means that it does not work. I think it works great.
2. This is good – though it does not quite fit the mood. The video is quite energetic but the music can be quite mellow at times.
3. Wow, this is not very good. I am sorry but the music and video do not line up at all – I do not understand what you have even tried to do.
4. I am not so sure about this I’m afraid. It is certainly not your best work.
5. This should do. I feel it fits the brief.
i: I am impressed with what you have done here. I cannot quite see what the director means that it does not work. I think it works great.
1st

Most of the comments given are quite negative. This one is positive and offers encouraging feedback. Words like ‘impressed’ and ‘great’ help intensify that positivity. Therefore, this ranks as the most positive of the bunch with 1st place.
This is good – though it does not quite fit the mood. The video is quite energetic but the music can be quite mellow at times.
2nd

Most of the comments given are quite negative. This one is positive though not the most positive. It is a little critical though it does suggest that it is ‘good’. Since it is positive but not the most positive, it best ranks as 2nd.
Wow, this is not very good. I am sorry but the music and video do not line up at all – I do not understand what you have even tried to do.
5th
This response is very negative. It is direct and rude, almost comically so. It displays no room for improvement or sympathy. As such, it is the lowest ranked response, 5th.
I am not so sure about this I’m afraid. It is certainly not your best work.
4th

This response is clearly disappointed. It is negative of the suggestion, but frustrating by the poor quality of track presented. Due to the soft language used, it is not the most negative. However, it must rank low, 4th.
This should do. I feel it fits the brief.
3rd
This is a very neutral response. The language is precise and unemotional. It feels neither positive nor negative. As such, it best suits the middlemost ranking, 3rd.

sets.p: My final review for the trailer is as follows: the video is panicky and unfocused. It made me feel anxious just watching. Fortunately, the music offset a lot of the stress on screen by providing mellow tones through most of the run-time. Clearly, there is a strange disjuncture between the director’s vision and the composer’s. At one minute in, the synchronisation of video and audio is so jarring that I am convinced they disagreed on style. By the end, I am left confused with how this trailer will adequately sell its TV series. It is a severe disappointment.
i: The composer and director have a shared vision.
False
False – Line 4 states that there is a ‘disjuncture’ between the vision of the composer and the vision of the director. As such, by definition, they do not have a shared vision.
The trailer was achieved on a cheap budget.
Cannot Say
Cannot Say – There is no mention of the budget in the passage. As such, we cannot say.
The trailer was designed for a film.
False

False – Line 6 states that the director was confused how the trailer will sells ‘its TV series’. This suggests that the trailer was designed for a TV series, not a film. Therefore, this statement is false.
The reviewer was unhappy with the trailer.
True

True – The passage can be summarised that the reviewer believes there was a disagreement between the director and composer in what they wanted the trailer to be. The final line states that the reviewer thought the trailer was a ‘severe disappointment’. Therefore, we can say it is true that the reviewer was unhappy with the trailer.
The music is panicky and unfocused.
False

False – Line 3 states that the music was mellow rather than panicky and unfocused. However, this is not to be confused with line 1 which states that the VIDEO is panicky and unfocused. Nonetheless, this statement is undoubtedly false.

sets.g: Passage A represents a formal and considered message. The language is serious and professional. The response to this message must equally be formal and kindly, though perhaps distant and deferential. Passage B represents a less formal message to the applicant. Though serious, it is more familiar and less strict in its use of language. It is likely that the sender and the applicant know each other at least a little bit. As such, the response is perhaps slightly bold, familiar in return.
sets.p:
A. After careful review of your performance during the six-week training programme, we feel that you require further examinations to better assess your ability. Please find the attached document that will detail the final interview process, which will assess whether you are an appropriate employee of our foundation.
B. Attached to this message are your training results. You have done well, though we think we need more info about your profile. Hope that is okay. If so, come to our interview next week – we will be interviewing others too so try not to be late.
i: Thanks for the heads up, I enjoyed the training programme so I’ll be there for the interview.
B
This response is quite casual. ‘Thanks’ is the more informal word of gratitude, and it does not offer any professional elements of language. Therefore, this is better suited for passage B.
I am greatly concerned that you feel my efforts shown during the training programme were not enough to convince you that I have the necessary skills for the job.
A

The language is professional and formal. The response attacks the issue without being too emotional connected to it, attempting instead to remain somewhat distant. Turns of phrases such as ‘feel my efforts’ and ‘not enough to convince you’ are not particularly casual uses of language. This is better suited for passage A.
That is a shame that you think I need an additional interview. I don’t really have the time to do it for the next few weeks, to be honest.
B
The language is quite flippant and unconcerned about professionalism. The final phrase, ‘to be honest’ is particularly casual – making this an appropriate response for passage B.
After careful consideration, I am afraid I must decline your offer for a further interview. I feel it would be a disservice to my skill set.
A
The language is very polite, such as ‘I am afraid’. The language is considered and formal. This is appropriate for passage A.
I appreciate the thoroughness of your assessment and I shall attend the interview for further examination.
A
The language is formal and reserved. The emotional distant in the statement indicates that this response is better suited to passage A.

sets.p: Thank you for attending the final / finale / finally interview in order to determine your place in our foundation. After must dispute, we can now announce that / the / though unfortunately, you were not successful in the process. Awhile / When / While your interview went well, your training results were mixed and not to the standard for / of / that we are currently looking for. Thank you so much for your effort and time give / put / you made into the process, we wish you the best of luck in the future.
i: “Thank you for attending the (final / finale / finally) interview…”
Final
Finale
Finally
A

‘Finale’ means the last part of a piece of entertainment, which is not appropriate here. ‘Finally’ interview does not make sense. However, the ‘final interview’, meaning the last interview to be done, is correct and is the right answer.
“…we can now announce (that / the / though) unfortunately…”
That
The
Though
A

‘The’ unfortunately does not make sense and therefore cannot be correct. ‘Though’ unfortunately does work, but in the context of the sentence is clumsy because it does not give its comparison that the word implies. ‘That’ unfortunately does not set up that problem, and works well – therefore is the correct answer.
“(Awhile / When / While) your interview went well
Awhile
When
While
C

‘Awhile’ denotes a time length which is incorrect and confusing here. ‘When’ your interview...’ sets up some further clause which is not provided and seems clumsy. ‘While’ sets up the right context to the phrase which is later reflected upon in the next phrase. Therefore, ‘while’ is the correct answer.
“…results were mixed and not to the standard (for / of / that) we are currently looking for.”
For
Of
That
C
‘For’ we, and ‘of’ we, do not make sense. ‘That’ we are…is the only reasonable answer and therefore must be the correct answer.
“Thank you so much for your effort and time you (give / made / put) into the process”
Give
Made
Put
C

‘Give’ is in the present tense and therefore is grammatical incorrect. ‘Gave’ would have worked but it is not an option. Be careful to notice the correct tense. ‘Made’ into the process is wonky and does not work very well. ‘Put’ into the process is the correct answer as it aptly describes the action that is expressed in the phrase.

sets.p: It sadness me deeply that I was unable to meet your standards. While I thought the interview process did well, there is little doubt that I struggled during the training programme. I believe I underestimated quiet how challenging some of those tasks was going to be. Nevertheless, thank you four the opportunity and being straight with me.
i: “It sadness me deeply…”
Saddens

It ‘sadness’ me does not make much sense. What we need to the third person present of the verb ‘to be sad’ which is ‘saddens’. Then, the sentence would say ‘it saddens me’ which is the correct use of language.
“While I thought the interview process did well,”
Went

‘Did’ well suggests that the interview itself was well – which seems bizarre and thus is incorrect. What we want is ‘went’ well, which says that the process was successful, or rather the person was successful rather than the abstract noun in itself.
“I believe I underestimated quiet how…”
Quite
This is a spelling error in the word ‘quiet’, which in this context does not make sense. We need ‘quite’ which softens the emphasis of the phrase making it correct.
“…some of those tasks was going to be.
Were
This is a grammatical error. The preceding noun, tasks, is plural and as such plural we need the plural past of ‘to be’ – were – rather than ‘was’.
“Nevertheless, thank you four the opportunity,”
For

This is a spelling error with the word ‘four’. This word is the number 4, which does not make sense. We need to delete the ‘u’, leaving ‘for’. ‘Thank you for the opportunity’ is a common turn of phrase which is the correct sentence here.

sets.p:
A man informed his friends that he was unsuccessful with a job application. The responses received from his friends are shown.

1. This is tricky. I do not believe you are skilled enough at your work to honestly get anything better.
2. Unfortunate outcome - though you are worth more than that position. I believe you will find a way through this.
3. Shame about the application, I thought you had it in the bag. Not to worry, something else will come along.
4. Right call on failing the application – you just weren’t good enough for the job.
5. Failing the application was a good thing, now you can look for something better!
i: This is tricky. I do not believe you are skilled enough at your work to honestly get anything better.
4th

The response is negative towards the individual which indicates that this message will rank low. Though critical, it is not unfairly harsh in context of the other responses. As such, it most appropriately ranks in 4th place.
Unfortunate outcome - though you are worth more than that position. I believe you will find a way through this.
1st
Given the generally negative messages on option, this one is positive in its outlook. It offers words of encouragement. With that, it should rank as the most positive, which is 1st.
Shame about the application, I thought you had it in the bag. Not to worry, something else will come along.
2nd
This response is friendly and positive. It offers comfort but not reinforcement. Being positive but not the most positive, it appropriately ranks as 2nd.
Right call on failing the application – you just weren’t good enough for the job.
5th
This is harsh in tone, almost jeering at the application. There is no room for sympathy and the language is negative. Therefore, this ranks as the most negative response; 5th place.
Failing the application was a good thing, now you can look for something better!
3rd
This response is bittersweet. It is trying to give positive support, but in a somewhat clumsy way. Given the context of the other responses, it most appropriates ranks in the middle at 3rd place.

sets.p: Applicant no. 58 struggled from the intensity of the six-week training process. Week 3, in particular, was of most concern. While the remaining applicants were able to navigate the athletic obstacles, this applicant collapsed from exhaustion. The emotional outbursts towards the staff on hand were disrespectful in the main. Fortunately, the rest of the training did not suffer any major challenges for any of the applicants. This incident at 15:40 on the 3rd of September was an unfortunate anomaly which reflected poorly on the character of an otherwise considered candidate.
i: The only applicant to struggle during the training was no. 42.
False
False – The applicant being referred to in the passage, the one that struggled during the training, was no.58 – as stated in line 1.
The applicant was disrespectful to the staff on hand on the 3rd of September.
True
True – Line 4 states that the applicant had emotional outbursts that were disrespectful towards the staff.
The applicant used foul language to the staff on hand.
Cannot Say
Cannot Say – Though in line 4 the passage states that the applicant was disrespectful towards the staff, there is no indication the they used foul language. Therefore, we cannot say.
The applicant suffered most from the athletic aspects of the training process.
True
True – Line 3 states that while the other applicants did not have a problem with the athletic obstacles, applicant no. 58 did and therefore suffered the most as they ‘collapsed from exhaustion’.
There were problems with some of the applicants on the seventh week.
False

False – There could not have been problems for applicants because the training process did not have a seventh week. While this seems like a ‘cannot say’, the answer is false because we can say conclusively that this statement is false.
